the cortical surface is covered with a dense network of microelectrocorticographic (μECOG) electrodes that are in close contact with cortical neurons.

1) micro-ECoG is a useful tool for studying the functional connectivity between neurons and the local field potential (LFP) and 2) the phase of the ECoG is correlated with the spiking activity of neurons in the same cortical region, while the amplitude of ECoG is not.

the development of a novel micro-electrocorticographic (micro-ECOG) electrode for chronic implantation and the investigation of the phase relationship between micro-ECOG and cortical neurons.
the relationship between the micro-electrocorticogram (mECOG) and the underlying cortical neurons.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the phase of cortical micro-electrocorticographic signals is related to the phase of the underlying cortical neurons, but the exact nature and strength of this relation depends on the frequency band, the type of neuron and the type of cortical area under consideration.
the phase relationship between the MEG/EEG and cortical neurons is not a straightforward one.
the phase relationship between micro-electrode and cortical neurons is not constant, but rather varies with time and location.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cortical micro-electrocorticogram (MEG) is the sum of the local field potential (LFP) and the electrocorticogram (ECoG) of a cortical region, and is the result of a complex interaction between cortical neurons and glia.
microelectrocorticography (μECoG) can provide a high-resolution measure of cortical activity.
the phase relationship between micro-electro-corticography (μECoG) and single neuron spiking is dependent on the neuron type and the type of stimulus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
micro-electrocorticographic recordings can provide a good estimate of cortical activity, which is useful for understanding the neural correlates of human cognition.
micro-ECoG is a promising technique to record the neural activity of the human brain with a spatial and temporal resolution similar to that of intracortical recordings.
micro-electrocorticographic (μECoG) recordings can provide high-quality, low-latency information about the spatio-temporal dynamics of neural activity.
